thread:
Samir: heads up - ACME asking for a packaged Reserved + Cushion offering. Key asks: predictability (single monthly invoice), P99 latency SLA (~<200ms), and ability to absorb ~30% bursts without procurement.
Maya: can you confirm their baseline vs peak token numbers and regions/compliance? quick bullet pls.
Sophie: ACME reply: baseline ~120M tokens/mo, peak days hit ~160M. US + EU regions. HIPAA flagged. They're open to 12mo commit if we provide a modest pre-bought cushion and reasonable overage terms.
Samir: notes from sales: target structure they want: 1) Reserved baseline (100M tokens) at committed rate. 2) Cushion credits pre-purchased (20-60M range) at a blended 'cushion' rate. 3) Overage above cushion billed at higher payg. 4) SLA for latency (they want guarantee). 5) Single monthly invoice.
Kira: pricing ops - we need a clear blended-rate formula and sample invoice. Proposed formula:
blended_rate = (reserved_rate*reserved_tokens + cushion_rate*cushion_tokens + overage_rate*overage_tokens) / total_tokens_used
Kira: quick example in K/K tokens:
```
reserved_rate = 0.012  # $ per K tokens
cushion_rate = 0.018
overage_rate = 0.030
# assume reserved=100K, cushion=30K, overage=10K => total usage 140K
print((reserved_rate*100 + cushion_rate*30 + overage_rate*10) / 140)
```
Maya: product questions: does this require a new SKU? new billing flow? UI for cushion balance + alerts? placement in offering matrix? launch criteria we need: HIPAA security signoff, latency acceptance tests, legal/billing terms, and rollback plan.
Jordan: infra perspective - to actually guarantee P99 <200ms for their model mix we need Dedicated capacity with pinned GPUs and reserved burst nodes. "Soft burst" via priority routing could help but cannot be SLA-backed. If ACME wants hard SLA we need pinned burst machines or capacity reservation.
Samir: ACME willing to pay ~20% uplift for hard SLA. Flag if that changes economics.
Kira: finance implications - selling cushion credits that sit unused affects revenue recognition and ARR. Need rules from RevOps. Also need an invoice template and clear SKU mapping.
Sophie: they want to run a pilot first: 3mo pilot suggested with smaller commit (12M reserved + 8M cushion) to validate latency and billing flows.
Maya: proposed product execution plan:
- design: define SKU + billing contract template + UI surfaces (cushion counter, alerts)
- security/compliance: HIPAA signoff and penetration checklist
- infra: Dedicated baseline + optional pinned burst nodes
- launch criteria: pilot complete (latency acceptance on >=90% days), legal and billing signoff, billing flow end-to-end tested
Maya: owners: Jordan -> infra config & cost estimate, Kira -> pricing model & finance sensitivity, Sophie -> pilot logistics & customer coordination, Maya -> product spec + acceptance criteria. Samir to own customer LOI.
Jordan: rough eng estimate: reuse reserved flow -> cushion tracking + billing hooks ~3-4 sprints. Pinned burst infra + SLA changes another ~2 sprints. Need detailed ticketing.
Kira: I'll run sensitivity models for token scenarios (100/120/150M) and produce blended unit economics + example invoices for finance.
Samir: I'll push ACME to sign LOI conditional on pilot. Sophie can we lock pilot dates?
Sophie: we'll propose pilot start in 3 weeks, 90 days duration. I'll send calendar invites after LOI.
billing-bot: invoice-draft generated for internal review: ACME pilot (12M reserved / 8M cushion) - DRAFT #3456
Samir: tagging @legal for HIPAA checklist and SOC docs. we'll need standard SAs + any addenda.
Maya: next actions: Kira to share model by EOD tomorrow; Jordan to confirm infra feasibility and cost estimate by week end; Sophie to secure pilot timeline; I'll draft product spec PR after Kira's numbers land.
Kira: ack. will include example invoice rows and a sample contract clause for cushion expiration/metering.
Jordan: also note ops: UI needs near-realtime cushion balance, alerting, and rate-limiting policies if cushion exhausted.
Samir: if cushion exhausted and overage kicks in ACME wants proactive alert + option to auto-top-up cushion credits.
Maya: include auto-top-up as optional feature in spec (opt-in) and contract language around top-ups and refunds.
Sophie: ACME also asked about rollback policy if SLA breached during pilot - we should commit to remediation SLAs and credits.
Kira: will model cost of credits/SLAs and suggested credit formulas for SLA failures.
Maya: great. thanks team :thumbsup:
